premise.claim: The backward-compat-test CI job was failing with `no space left on device` when loading Docker images to the kind cluster (~36 MB free, not enough for `docker save` temp files).
premise.evidence: June-2026 failure logs are past GitHub's 90-day retention and cannot be re-inspected. Corroborated historically: master merged the same class of fix for kind-e2e as #6123 (5438f7a43, 2026-07-14, 'prevent out-of-disk failures'). On current master the symptom is NOT observable: backward-compat job 126560263055 (run 41825854539, 2026-11-04) shows /dev/root 145G with 85G avail before build and 81-82G after (results/external/master-backcompat-disk.txt); the only recent backward-compat failures (run 41981311011, 2026-11-05) are a go.mod>=1.26 vs Go 1.25 toolchain error, not disk (results/external/dependabot-failure-mode.txt). Not blocking per policy (not-reproduced != refuted; cheap standard hardening with maintainer precedent).

liveNote: L3 (real GHA runner) intentionally skipped: no local docker/kind on the review machine, and the change is self-testing in CI — the workflow under review executes the new step on every PR run. A fresh backward-compat + kind-e2e run on the merged/rebased state is the live-layer evidence (see review.acceptance A-CI).
